name: Bow and barb
description:
Two animals that are useless apart. The bow-caste is a crossbow laid flat: a stock running the way it travels, head at the leading end, and two prod-limbs thrown out sideways from the shoulders, tapering to feelers. It has nothing to hurt anything with. The barb-caste lies in the groove down the middle of that stock — a hard point on an abdomen full of something that goes off, and no way of getting anywhere. One winds, the other lands, and both are spent in the same second, which is why neither is drawn to survive it and why the hive only ever sends them in volleys.

There is no string. One was drawn, tip to tip, because something had to explain where the throw came from — and what it explained it with was a bright orange bar across the middle of the animal, which is the loudest thing on a body whose loudest thing should be the core about to go off. The limbs rolling under the load and the barb hauling back down the groove say the same thing and say it in the body. What is left of the prod is pulled toward a pair of antennae: longer, much thinner, tapering to a point and kicked forward at the tip, so the station reads as something the animal feels the air with — which is what a beetle actually wears there.

It was a longbow first, stood on end with the barb strung across its middle. That read as a frame and not as an animal facing anywhere, which is the one thing it cannot afford: a longbow is the same shape from either end, and this field is drawn top-down where a body needs a nose. A crossbow has a front. Laid flat it is a body plan an insect can carry without being asked to — long thorax, head at the leading end, limbs out from the shoulders — and the prod sits forward on the stock so most of the animal is behind the thing that throws, which reads as travelling rather than as a bow that happens to be lying down.

Two lit scent organs on one sprite is the tell that this is two creatures and not one with a decoration, and it costs nothing to say it: the shared organ is already what every body in this roster carries. The barb's rides the neck ahead of its core, because a thing with a point has a front and the lit end belongs at it; the bow's rides its own head.

Shapes this could fall back into, all of them tried. Prod-limbs curled to a brace height of 0.45 of the tip-to-tip span came out a horseshoe, then a snail. A sac cut off a shaft at the waist put two ink outlines across each other and the seam read as a join in the middle of an animal, so the point is laid under a closed sac instead, rear buried, and the sac swallows it as it fills.

The windup is the point. The barb hauls back down the groove while both prod-limbs roll under the load and its core swells — which is the yellow flash the game used to paint over this sprite, drawn instead. On release the bow unwinds through rest and past it while the barb keeps going, because it has left the string. Nothing here points down the line it is about to take: the sprite only ever flips and never rotates, so an arrowhead would promise a heading the engine cannot keep. Drawn facing +x. Same id and radius 10.

loosed.description: The barb alone, in flight. Everything the bow was is gone from it, because the bow did not come — that is the whole point of there being two animals. Recentred on its own body: the canvas is sized for a pair, so left where it lay in the groove it would fly a third of a body off its own hitbox.

planted.description: The barb after it has landed and before it goes off. The same two parts it flew as, standing in a scorch it put there arriving, with the core already swollen past anything the windup asked for. The half-second it holds this is the half-second the player has to not be here.

spent.description: The bow after it has let go, left lying where it loosed. Prod-limbs fallen open past rest, antennae slack, stock drained, scent organ down to `faint` — it has nothing left to throw and about a second before it stops signalling. Drawn so the field keeps a record of where a volley came from.

walk.description:
carrying it into range. Six legs on an alternating tripod — front and back of one side swinging with the middle of the other, the two sets half a cycle apart — which is the gait the leg count implies and the one that reads as walking rather than as paddling. The prod breathes against its own tension over the top of it, because a loaded bow is never slack, and the barb rides a little of the draw down its groove: the pair is carried, not dragged. The two organs pulse out of phase with each other, because they are two animals.

This used to be a held pose on the theory that the pair does not walk. It does — the approach is most of the time it is alive, and it spent all of that standing still.

fuse.description:
landed, and filling. Four pumps across the half-second, each one leaving the sac bigger than the last let it settle back to — so the shape is a ratchet rather than a pulse, and what you read is pressure going in rather than a light blinking. It peaks on the final frame at three quarters again its own size, because the frame after this one is the blast. The core runs ahead of the sac the whole way, since the core is what is swelling and the sac is only what is failing to contain it, and it dims on each intake and comes back brighter — the one thing here that still reads at 1.35x on a crowded screen. The point is pushed out as the sac takes it, so it stays proud of the thing consuming it.

The sac is authored about its own middle, which is the only reason a scale on it is a swell rather than a stretch along the body. Its duration is the game's fuse; feelers stretches playback to `fuseTime`, so re-timing one re-times the other.

Only ever baked under `planted`. On the base body it would be a bow that never let go watching its own barb fill, which is not a state this creature has.

coil.description: the windup, stretched to the game's telegraph. The barb hauls back down the groove while both limbs roll under the load and the core swells — the load is the only thing left saying a throw is coming, now that there is no string to draw. Wound rather than eased: a fast first draw, a slow creep against the load, a settle, a last snatch. Holds on the final frame, because the release is the throw.

strike.description: the release, and the only one of these that is not symmetrical. It opens on the coil's last frame exactly, so the handover reads as the same motion continuing rather than a cut. The bow unwinds through neutral, past it, and settles; the barb does not come back at all, because it has left the string — it lunges a full length forward and holds there. Baked from `spent` as well, where the barb tracks have nothing to move and what plays is a bow unwinding onto nothing.
